definition: TensorRT is a software development kit (SDK) and inference optimization runtime developed by Nvidia for deploying trained deep learning and machine learning models on graphics processing units (GPUs).
details: It can import models from frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and ONNX, and compile them into optimized runtime engines for low-latency and high-throughput inference. In current Nvidia documentation, the TensorRT name is also used for a broader product family that includes the core TensorRT SDK, TensorRT-LLM, and TensorRT-RTX. The core SDK is primarily a proprietary Nvidia product, although Nvidia also maintains Apache-licensed open-source TensorRT repositories and related companion projects.

explainer.lead: TensorRT is Nvidia's SDK and runtime for deploying trained models on GPUs. It matters because it turns framework models into engines built for low-latency, high-throughput inference.

tiers.eli5: Think of a model as a recipe written for any kitchen; TensorRT rewrites it so one particular chef can cook it as fast as possible.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers import models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, or ONNX and compile them into optimized runtime engines. A pitfall is assuming an engine is portable: compatibility depends on GPU and library versions.
tiers.paperLevel: No formula; it is a compilation and inference-optimization runtime rather than a learning algorithm. Its limits come from the target hardware and the supported model formats.

explainer.example: A team exports a trained PyTorch model to ONNX and compiles it into a TensorRT engine, then serves it on GPUs for low-latency inference.
